amendments.normalized_body: Restore a directional assertion in `run_probe_chemistry_stress_with_suffix` that verifies actual molt failures or failed-molt accumulation occur under low-GH + high-NO₂ conditions. The diff removes the check (`if molt_failures == 0 && final_state.animal.failed_molt_accum <= 0.0 { record_failure(...) }`) but the scenario's doc comment still promises "molt failures, increased mortality, condition decline". Without this assertion, the probe only validates elevated `molt_stress_index > 0.2`, mortality, and condition decline — but not that molts actually fail. If the current model doesn't reliably produce these events, either (a) soften the assertion to check `molt_stress > threshold OR failed_molt_accum > 0` as a weaker directional claim, or (b) update the doc comment to drop the "molt failures" claim.

Consider gating the `projected_carbonate_equilibrium()` call inside `emit_tick_snapshot` (engine.rs:122-124) behind a higher verbosity level or computing it less frequently (e.g. only on daily ticks). This solver runs on every tick when tracing is enabled, including the breeding scenario's ~1500 ticks. If the carbonate equilibrium solve is nontrivial, this could materially slow down instrumented probe runs.
